extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners (primary) and patent applicants/agents (secondary)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners on issuing notices of grounds for rejection, handling amendments and translations (international applications), determining whether applicants were given opportunity to respond, and classifying/issuing non-final vs final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of international applications and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a prior-filed application serving as a domestic priority claim is an international application, inventions commonly stated in both the domestic-priority-claiming application and the prior-filed international application (limited to specification, claims, or drawings submitted at the international filing date) are considered filed at the international filing date. Korean translation of PCT Articles 19/34 written amendments submitted within the reference date are treated as voluntary amendments under Article 47 of the Patent Act. An examiner may request copies of documents cited in the ISR/IPER where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope of inventions of an international application relied upon as 'another application' is limited to the inventions described in the specification, claims or drawings of the international application as of the international filing date and its translation; rules differ depending on filing date (before/after Jan 1, 2015). An international application deemed withdrawn for failure to file Korean translation within the specified period cannot be treated as 'another application' for enlarged-concept-of-novelty purposes. For amendments of foreign-language international applns, amended matters are limited to those described in the original document or its Korean translation as of filing; care must be taken when determining added matter under Article 208(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify grounds for rejection and opportunity to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Act (Article 62) requires that, before making a decision to reject, the examiner must notify the applicant of the grounds for rejection and give an opportunity to submit a written argument within a designated period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects against examiner error and ensures fairness under First-to-File. The notice-and-opportunity requirement is foundational to rejection procedure and triggers the timelines and types of subsequent actions (non-final, final necessitated by amendment, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory categories of grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The grounds for rejection include: ① the claimed invention is not patentable pursuant to Articles 25, 29, 32, 36(1),(3) or 44; ② application filed by person not entitled under Article 33(1) or claimed invention not patentable under the proviso of that Article; ③ violation of Treaty provisions; ④ failure to satisfy requirements in Article 42(3)(i), (4), (8) or Article 45; ⑤ an amendment is out of scope prescribed in Article 47(2); ⑥ a divisional filed out of scope (Article 52(1)); ⑦ a converted application filed out of scope (Article 53(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When issuing a notice, the examiner should reference the relevant statutory provisions (see 5.1(2)). These categories frame reasons for non-final or final rejection and for refusing to enter amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated period for submission of written argument
rubrics_metrics.description: The period designated for submission of the argument shall be within two months regardless of whether an applicant is overseas resident or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If written argument requires tests and result evaluations with recognized time consumption, additional period may be added. Note: the Commissioner-designated period for an amendment request under Article 46 is within one month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete notification of all discovered grounds (default rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for special cases, all grounds for rejection discovered during examination shall be notified in a complete manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To protect applicants' procedural interests and expedite examination, an examiner shall notify all grounds of rejection altogether, including potentially conflicting grounds. Exceptions are outlined (see next entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — incomprehensible claims due to lack of clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Where contents of a claimed invention cannot be comprehended due to lack of clarity in the description, the examiner shall notify only the ground(s) for rejection under Article 42(3) or (4) without conducting prior art search or assessing novelty/inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if the lack of clarity is insignificant such that understanding is possible, the examiner shall conduct prior art search and review patentability to the extent of comprehension, and notify those grounds together with Article 42(3),(4) violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — certain grounds to be notified without patentability assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is certain that a claim has newly added matter, or where uncertainty exists under Article 32 (e.g., contravention of public order), or where it is clear the claim is not a statutory subject matter or not industrially applicable, the examiner shall notify those grounds for rejection without judging novelty or inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are grounds that can be addressed independently of patentability assessments and should be raised immediately in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — failure of unity (Article 45) handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application fails to satisfy the single-patent requirement under Article 45, the examiner shall examine inventions that fall within a single group and notify grounds discovered through that examination, along with the rejection ground regarding lack of unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For efficient examination, the examiner may notify the Article 45 violation before judging other patentability requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and specificity of notices — stipulate provisions and claim-level basis
rubrics_metrics.description: When notifying a ground for rejection, the examiner shall stipulate the relevant provisions of the Act or laws. For multiple claims, grounds for rejection should be indicated on a claim-by-claim basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details on claim-level examination are referenced in Section 5.4; notices should make it clear which claim each ground pertains to to enable focused applicant response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and evidentiary support required in notices
rubrics_metrics.description: The grounds for rejection shall be stated with definite, concise, normal sentences to help an applicant's understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particular requirements: (i) for prior art used in inventive step, rely on the minimum number of references necessary and identify the parts of the references used as basis; (ii) when denying novelty or inventive step by asserting public knowledge/practice, specifically state facts showing public knowledge/practice; (iii) when asserting failure to meet written description requirements, specify the deficient parts and corresponding reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive-step rejection must explain differences to closest prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: When notifying rejection for lack of inventive step, the examiner shall clearly describe the difference between the invention recited in the claims and the closest prior art reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if both lack of novelty and lack of inventive step are notified together, the examiner may follow the novelty assessment method for the novelty ground and may notify inventive-step rejection on the logic that a skilled person could easily make the invention from the prior art (i.e., where the claimed invention is identical to the prior art). See Part 3, Chapter 3, 5.1 for inventive step assessment procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestion of divisional or conversion in notice
rubrics_metrics.description: If considered necessary for the convenience of an applicant and for expeditious and accurate examination, an examiner may suggest a division or conversion of an application in the notice of rejection grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must indicate that the suggestion has no legal effect and that the decision to carry out division or conversion is up to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of erroneous notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a written notice of rejection contains errors in writing, the examiner shall issue a corrected notice of grounds for rejection again, regardless of whether an applicant submits a written argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions where re-issuance is not required: (i) where the applicant is deemed to have submitted a written argument based on his/her correct understanding of the errors; (ii) where the applicant did not submit any arguments and the errors are clerical and not influential to the examiner's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling self-evident errors in the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the specification contains a self-evident error in writing, the examiner shall notify the error as 'Considerations' if there are other grounds for rejection. If there are no other grounds, the examiner shall communicate with the applicant (e.g., by telephone) and may advise the applicant to voluntarily amend or may amend ex officio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any advice or guidance given by communication media should be documented in 'Applicant/Agent Personal Interview' in the Examination Report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection without additional notice when grounds substantially coincide
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner finds it appropriate to maintain a rejection which has been notified with consideration of any amendments, the examiner may decide to reject without issuing an additional notice of other rejection grounds which exist but were not previously notified, provided the decision to reject substantially coincides with previously-notified grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial coincidence is evaluated from the perspective of whether the applicant was practically given an opportunity to submit arguments; this is not confined to identical wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to reject based on same claim when prior opportunity provided
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision to reject an application may be made when the claimed invention still lacks novelty or inventive step over the same reference(s) relied upon in the original notice and the applicant has had an opportunity to submit written arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In principle, rejection is permissible when (①) the concerned claim is rejected under the same statutory provision and (②) the claim lacks novelty/inventive step over the same reference or same combination of references. Example: claim amended by adding an element described in the description but still lacks inventive step over the same reference — rejection can be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to reject based on other claims (identity/substantial identity)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim under examination is amended to be identical (including 'substantially identical') to another claim which was rejected, a decision to reject the amended claim can be made on the basis of the grounds previously notified to the other claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show amended claim becoming identical to previously-rejected claim or adding limitations of another rejected claim; in such cases a rejection decision based on prior notice is allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When amendment necessitates a new ground (new combination of references)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment causes the need to rely on a new combination of references to reject the amended claim, a new ground of rejection is considered necessary and, depending on the stage of examination, the examiner shall issue a second office action (non-final) or refuse to enter the amendment and continue examination with the original claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate cases where amendments introduce elements requiring new reference combinations. If the new combination arose from simple errors in a prior notice, the examiner should refuse entry of the amendment rather than issue a decision to reject based on the new combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling newly added claims by amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: A new claim created by amendment, to which no ground of rejection had been previously issued, generally necessitates that an opportunity for submission of written arguments be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if the new claim is identical to a claim to which a ground of rejection had been previously issued (including substantial identity), a decision to reject may be made without providing a fresh opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination whether applicant was given opportunity re: description deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a term or phrase found to be indefinite in a claim is changed by amendment, the applicant may not be considered to have had a realistic opportunity to respond (they could amend without recognizing the deficiency), and thus a decision to reject cannot be made without special circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only where the amended claim still fails to overcome the previously-notified ground and the claim language substantially coincides with the previously-notified language may rejection proceed without a new opportunity. Examples clarify when non-final vs final rejection should be issued depending on whether claim language changed and whether prior-notified deficient language persists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of notice: non-final rejection vs final rejection necessitated by amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of grounds for rejection are categorized as: (a) non-final rejection — issued for the first time or where grounds do not arise from amendments necessitating a final rejection by amendment; (b) final rejection necessitated by amendment — rejection necessitated by amendments made in response to a previously issued rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-final rejection may be issued regardless of voluntary amendments if it relates to unamended portions, if post-amendment claims still have grounds that stem from pre-amendment description, or where grounds arose for reasons other than amendments. Examples demonstrate when non-final rejection should be used.
